//: Add these to the settings of the Claude Code sessions you drive chargehand from, not the runner's. ~/.claude/settings.json covers every session you start; a project's shared .claude/settings.json holds its allow rules until you trust the folder. `status` runs without a prompt, because by default it prints only identifiers, states, timings and URLs. Everything else here asks, and an ask rule prompts in every permission mode, auto and bypassPermissions included: every mutating command, and the two reads that bring untrusted text into the session, `logs` and `--verbose-titles`.
//rules: Each ask rule leads with a wildcard rather than anchoring on the program name. A Bash rule matches the command text, not the program behind it, so an anchored 'Bash(chargehand cancel:*)' gates 'chargehand cancel X' and misses both '/usr/local/bin/chargehand cancel X' and "sh -c 'chargehand cancel X'". An assistant that ran 'which chargehand' and used the answer produces the second form without trying to evade anything. The allow rule stays anchored on purpose: a read that falls outside it prompts, which is the harmless direction to fail in.
